testName: Class B Knowledge Test #1 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a crime that disqualifies someone from getting a hazardous materials endorsement?
questions.explanation: Several crimes will disqualify you from getting a hazardous materials endorsement for seven years. These include arson, robbery, and crimes involving dishonesty, fraud, or lying. More serious crimes like murder result in a lifetime ban.

questions.question: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must provide:

options.text: A list of countries you visited in the last 10 years.
Your work history for the past five years.

questions.explanation: To get a hazardous materials endorsement, you must submit your fingerprints and pass a TSA background check.

questions.question: Poor weight balance:

options.text: Can make the vehicle harder to control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can make the vehicle harder to control.
questions.explanation: Poorly balanced cargo makes a vehicle difficult to handle. Pay attention to how you distribute weight when loading cargo.

questions.question: Using a hand-held mobile device while driving is:

options.text: Okay if the weather is clear.
Allowed if it is for work.

questions.explanation: Using a hand-held phone while driving a commercial vehicle is illegal and unsafe.

questions.question: What is tire load?

options.text: The highest air pressure allowed in a tire
The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a certain pressure
The minimum safe weight a tire must carry
The average weight of all tires on a vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum safe weight a tire can carry at a certain pressure
questions.explanation: Tire load is the maximum safe weight a tire can hold at a certain pressure. You can find this number printed on the side of the tire.

questions.question: What does a vehicle inspection report do?

options.text: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.
Can take the place of flat mirrors.
Help you see a wider area.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see a wider area.
questions.explanation: Many large vehicles have curved convex mirrors. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, they also make objects look smaller and farther away than they actually are.

questions.question: Cargo with a high center of gravity:

options.text: Makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.
Is good to use in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Makes a vehicle more likely to tip over.
questions.explanation: Cargo with a high center of gravity makes a vehicle more likely to tip than cargo with a low center of gravity. Keep cargo weight as low as possible to reduce this risk.

questions.question: When driving down a hill:
questions.explanation: When a vehicle goes downhill, gravity pulls it forward and increases its speed.

questions.question: When you leave your vehicle, you should:
questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: What type of force must emergency brakes use?
questions.explanation: Air pressure can leak away over time. So emergency brakes in an air brake system must use mechanical force to work.

questions.question: What do federal and state laws require?

options.text: Drivers to inspect their vehicles regularly.
Drivers to inspect their vehicles only if they think there may be a problem.
Drivers to inspect their vehicles only if traveling out-of-state.
Drivers to inspect their vehicles only if transporting hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers to inspect their vehicles regularly.
questions.explanation: Commercial drivers must inspect their vehicles before every trip. Regular inspections help find problems early before they become dangerous or expensive.

questions.question: What equipment should a commercial motor vehicle have?

options.text: A fire extinguisher only if transporting hazardous materials.
A fire extinguisher only if traveling through remote areas.
A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.

questions.correctAnswerText: A fire extinguisher and other emergency equipment.
questions.explanation: All commercial motor vehicles must have proper emergency equipment. This includes spare fuses, three reflective warning triangles or flares, and at least one working fire extinguisher.

questions.question: If your wheels spin when accelerating on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Take your foot off the accelerator.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take your foot off the accelerator.
questions.explanation: If your drive wheels start to spin while accelerating on a slippery surface, remove your foot from the accelerator.

questions.question: If you need to add coolant to a system without a recovery tank, what should you do first?

options.text: Keep the engine running while adding coolant.
Do not use gloves when touching the radiator cap.
Wait for the engine to cool down before adding coolant.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the engine to cool down before adding coolant.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine and wait until it cools before adding coolant. Use gloves or a thick cloth to protect your hands. Turn the radiator cap slowly to the first stop to release pressure.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Allow the rear wheels to lock up
Allow all wheels to lock up
Alert other drivers when you are braking

questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents your wheels from locking up when you brake hard on a slippery surface.

questions.question: Hanging meat as cargo is usually:
questions.explanation: Hanging meat cargo is unstable because the meat swings during transport and its center of gravity is high.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with air brakes, you should check that the ____ activate automatically when air pressure drops below 45 psi.
questions.explanation: Before driving, verify that spring brakes activate automatically when air pressure drops between 20 and 45 psi. Chock the wheels and release air by pressing the brake pedal repeatedly. When pressure gets too low, the parking brake valve pops out and spring brakes engage.

questions.question: When backing into an alley on the right side of your vehicle, what should you do first?

options.text: Drive directly into the alley parking space.
Turn right to position yourself directly in front of the alley.
Pass the alley and stop perpendicular to the outer boundary.
Pass the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pass the alley and stop parallel to the outer boundary.
questions.explanation: When alley docking, pass the alley first and stop parallel to the outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space.

questions.question: When leaving your vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Use the parking brake only if the vehicle is on a slope.
Do not use the parking brake, as it can damage the tires.

questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when parking. Do not use it if your brakes are very hot or if they are wet and it is freezing.

questions.question: Which is an example of required emergency equipment?
questions.explanation: Commercial motor vehicles must have emergency equipment. This includes spare electrical fuses, three red reflective triangles or six fuses or three flares, and at least one charged fire extinguisher.

questions.question: Hydraulic brakes can fail for one of two reasons. Which one is listed below?

options.text: The brakes are used too much in one day

questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failures happen for two main reasons. First, overusing brakes on downhill grades causes them to fade. Second, loss of hydraulic pressure in the braking system occurs. Well-maintained brakes rarely fail, but know what to do if they do.

questions.question: Which of the following may result in being denied a hazardous materials endorsement?

options.text: Not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
Having a speeding conviction within the previous three years
Not answering every question correctly on the hazardous materials test
Not passing the hazardous materials test on the first attempt

questions.correctAnswerText: Not being a lawful permanent resident of the United States
questions.explanation: You will be denied a hazardous materials endorsement if you renounce U.S. citizenship, are not a lawful permanent resident, are wanted or indicted for certain felonies, are judged mentally unfit, or are considered a security threat by the Transportation Security Administration (TSA).

questions.question: Dual tires should:
questions.explanation: When inspecting your vehicle, make sure dual tires do not touch each other or any other part of the vehicle.

questions.question: A distracted driver:

options.text: Is usually aware of what is happening around them
Is a good person to follow

questions.explanation: Distracted driving causes slower perception, delayed decisions, and wrong actions. Watch for distracted drivers and avoid them when possible.

questions.question: When traveling down a hill, switch to a lower gear:

options.text: As you go downhill and pick up speed
Near the bottom of the hill

questions.explanation: Always downshift before going downhill. Shifting an automatic transmission to a lower gear at high speed can damage it and cause you to lose engine braking. Choose a safe speed based on the hill's steepness and length, your vehicle's weight, road conditions, and weather.

questions.question: When traveling with cargo, you must check that it is secure:

options.text: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving
Only after traveling up a hill
Only after coming to a hard stop

questions.correctAnswerText: Every 150 miles or three hours of driving
questions.explanation: Check cargo before starting, within the first 50 miles, and every three hours or 150 miles. The driver is responsible for keeping cargo safely secured throughout the trip.

questions.question: Which is NOT an example of a distracted person motorists should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to a passenger in their vehicle
A child on the side of the road
A construction worker on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Be careful near people not paying attention to the road. Watch for construction workers, drivers talking to passengers, and children near the road.

questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe if a professional did the repairs
Safe if the repair looks solid

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are not safe. Replace them before driving the vehicle.

questions.question: How can you reduce stress while driving?
questions.explanation: Stress can lead to aggressive driving, which is dangerous. Playing calming music can help you relax if you feel stressed while driving.

questions.question: When you leave a vehicle unattended, what should you do?

options.text: Set the parking brake only if parked on a slope.
Let air out of the tires by 10 percent.

questions.explanation: Always set the parking brake when you leave your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do to prevent fatigue while driving?
questions.explanation: Heat and poor ventilation make you sleepy. Open a window, use a vent, or turn on air conditioning to keep cool and stay alert.

questions.question: During the basic vehicle control skills test, how are pull-ups handled?

options.text: You lose points for each pull-up.
You are allowed three pull-ups per maneuver.
A pull-up earns points only if you exit the vehicle first.
Only too many pull-ups count as errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only too many pull-ups count as errors.
questions.explanation: During the test, one pull-up does not count against you. However, too many pull-ups will be marked as errors.

questions.question: Which of these is a sign of drowsy driving?

options.text: Your eyes go out of focus by themselves.
You have trouble keeping your head up.
You drift from lane to lane.

questions.explanation: Signs of drowsiness include eyes closing or losing focus on their own, difficulty holding your head up, and drifting between lanes.

questions.question: What is true about broken suspension parts?
questions.explanation: The suspension system supports the vehicle and keeps the axles in place. Broken parts in this system are very dangerous.

questions.question: What is not allowed with regrooved tires?

options.text: They cannot be used on any vehicle.
They cannot be used on the front of a bus.
They cannot be used on trucks carrying gravel.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot be used on the front of a bus.
questions.explanation: Regrooved, recapped, or retreaded tires are not allowed on the front wheels of a bus.

questions.question: What is true about rims with welding repairs?

options.text: They are not safe to use.
They are safe to use on rear tires.
They are safe to use if carrying a light load.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are not safe to use.
questions.explanation: Wheels or rims with welding repairs are never safe and should never be used.

questions.question: What should you do when driving down a steep hill?

options.text: Press the brakes the whole way down.
Shift into a higher gear to slow down.
Shift into lower gears to slow down.
Put the truck in neutral to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift into lower gears to slow down.
questions.explanation: On a steep hill, use the engine's braking power to slow down. Use your brakes only to supplement this method to prevent overheating.

questions.question: Reading a text message while driving is:

options.text: Allowed only if you are not pulling a trailer.

questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is dangerous and illegal.

questions.question: What is another name for front-end header boards?
questions.explanation: Front-end header boards are also called "headache racks." They protect the driver from cargo that moves forward during a crash or sudden stop.

questions.question: If there is a cargo fire in a box trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Put a large, heavy blanket over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen, which makes the fire grow larger.

questions.question: When air tanks reach 125 psi, what does the air compressor governor do?

options.text: Stop pumping air into the tanks.
Start pumping air into the tanks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop pumping air into the tanks.
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when air pressure reaches 125 psi. This pressure level is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: If you stop on the road or shoulder, what must you do within 10 minutes?

options.text: Stand behind your vehicle and wave traffic past you.

questions.explanation: You must place emergency warning devices, like reflective triangles, within 10 minutes of stopping on the road or shoulder.

questions.question: While driving, what should a driver pay attention to?

options.text: Only the front of the vehicle.
Only the front and sides, not behind.

questions.explanation: You must be aware of everything happening around your vehicle at all times. Check your mirrors on both sides regularly while driving.

questions.question: During the basic control skills test, when can you exit the vehicle?

options.text: You are not allowed to exit the vehicle.
You are discouraged from exiting the vehicle.
You can exit only if the vehicle is in reverse.
You can exit only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can exit only if the vehicle is in neutral and the parking brake is set.
questions.explanation: During the basic control skills test, put the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake before exiting. You can check the vehicle's position no more than twice (once during straight-line backing).

questions.question: Before you try to put out an engine fire, what should you do?

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up remaining fuel.

questions.explanation: Turn off the engine as soon as it is safe to do so if you have an engine fire. Do not open the hood when trying to put out the fire.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you do?

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.explanation: Get out of the way of an aggressive driver. Do not make eye contact, do not speed up to challenge them, and do not react to their angry gestures.

questions.question: When checking automatic transmission fluid, what might you need to do?
questions.explanation: Some vehicles require you to leave the engine running to check the automatic transmission fluid level.

questions.question: In a newer vehicle, how do you apply the parking brake?
questions.explanation: In newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake is controlled by a diamond-shaped yellow knob. Pull it out to apply the brakes and push it in to release them.

questions.question: What is the maximum air leakage rate for a triple combination vehicle during an applied leakage test?
questions.explanation: A triple combination vehicle must not lose more than 6 psi per minute during an applied leakage test.
